evidence.claim: On the prime minister's directions, the finance minister pursued targeted subsidy proposals to provide immediate relief to lower-income households under a PM relief package.
evidence.title: Federal Minister for Finance and Revenue presided over a meeting on PM Relief Package through USC
evidence.publisher: Ministry of Finance, Government of Pakistan
evidence.excerpt: On the prime minister's directions, the finance minister pursued targeted subsidy proposals to provide immediate relief to lower-income households under a PM relief package.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Official government release with direct policy description and named participants.
evidence.period_fit: Directly within the target year and while Sharif's cabinet was defining its economic response.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Directly tied to Sharif's directions, though implementation ran through the finance and social safety ministries.
contrary_evidence: The release is a policy announcement, not proof of successful delivery at scale.

evidence.claim: The government said it would raise taxes on the rich, ban some government vehicle purchases, and target a 4.9 percent fiscal deficit while seeking IMF bailout support.
evidence.title: Pakistan to raise taxes on rich, ban some car buying to secure IMF bailout
evidence.excerpt: The government said it would raise taxes on the rich, ban some government vehicle purchases, and target a 4.9 percent fiscal deficit while seeking IMF bailout support.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Reuters budget reporting on a concrete fiscal package with explicit targets.
evidence.period_fit: Directly within the target year and the FY2022-23 budget window.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Government policy under Sharif and finance minister Miftah Ismail; the budget was a coalition decision, not a one-man act.
contrary_evidence: The package was clearly shaped by IMF pressure and austerity needs rather than unconstrained domestic choice.

evidence.claim: The budget speech said the government chose difficult decisions over political convenience, prioritized economic stability, proposed special taxes on higher incomes, created a task force against tax leakage, and imposed austerity on vehicle and foreign-travel spending.
evidence.title: Budget Speech 2022-23
evidence.publisher: Ministry of Finance, Government of Pakistan
evidence.excerpt: The budget speech said the government chose difficult decisions over political convenience, prioritized economic stability, proposed special taxes on higher incomes, created a task force against tax leakage, and imposed austerity on vehicle and foreign-travel spending.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Primary budget speech from the finance ministry with explicit policy commitments.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Attributed to Sharif's government and budget team; some wording is rhetorical, but it reflects the government's public policy line.
contrary_evidence: Speech rhetoric can overstate intent relative to later execution.

evidence.claim: The FY2022-23 budget was framed as a sustainable-growth budget built around widening the tax net, reducing the fiscal deficit, protecting vulnerable groups, continuing the IMF programme, targeting subsidies, and increasing taxes on wealthy people.
evidence.title: Budget in Brief 2022-23
evidence.publisher: Ministry of Finance, Government of Pakistan
evidence.excerpt: The FY2022-23 budget was framed as a sustainable-growth budget built around widening the tax net, reducing the fiscal deficit, protecting vulnerable groups, continuing the IMF programme, targeting subsidies, and increasing taxes on wealthy people.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Primary budget summary document with concrete policy priorities and fiscal strategy.
evidence.period_fit: Directly within the target year and the FY2022-23 policy cycle.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Government policy under Sharif's coalition; broader macro conditions and IMF constraints are separate from the ruler's stated priorities.
contrary_evidence: It is a plan document, so implementation has to be checked elsewhere.

evidence.claim: The finance ministry said the CCoP welcomed revival plans for Pakistan Steel Mills through foreign direct investment and technology transfer, and also discussed recapitalizing NPPMCL and private participation in DISCO management to improve viability and service quality.
evidence.title: Federal Minister for Finance and Revenue chaired a meeting of Cabinet Committee on Privatisation
evidence.publisher: Ministry of Finance, Government of Pakistan
evidence.excerpt: The finance ministry said the CCoP welcomed revival plans for Pakistan Steel Mills through foreign direct investment and technology transfer, and also discussed recapitalizing NPPMCL and private participation in DISCO management to improve viability and service quality.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Official record of a cabinet committee meeting with concrete industrial and utility-sector actions.
evidence.period_fit: Directly within 2022 and under Sharif's government.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Attributed to the Sharif cabinet's economic team; final outcomes depended on later implementation and private-sector response.
contrary_evidence: The measures are reform proposals and committee decisions, not completed restructuring.

evidence.claim: The IMF said the FY2023 budget aimed for an underlying primary surplus of 0.4 percent of GDP, backed by current-spending restraint, higher-income tax mobilization, protected development spending, and a market-determined exchange rate, while expanding social safety and reforming SOEs.
evidence.title: IMF Reaches Staff-Level Agreement on the Combined Seventh and Eighth Reviews for Pakistan's Extended Fund Facility
evidence.excerpt: The IMF said the FY2023 budget aimed for an underlying primary surplus of 0.4 percent of GDP, backed by current-spending restraint, higher-income tax mobilization, protected development spending, and a market-determined exchange rate, while expanding social safety and reforming SOEs.
evidence.source_locator: press release text and bullet list on policy priorities
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Primary IMF statement contemporaneous with the policy package and program review.
evidence.period_fit: Directly within 2022, during Sharif's first budget and IMF negotiations.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Attributed to the Sharif-led authorities, but shaped by IMF conditionality and provincial bargaining; the central bank retained institutional independence.
contrary_evidence: The IMF also described FY22 overheating, large deficits, and rising inflation as inherited or policy-induced problems.

evidence.claim: The IMF said Pakistan's authorities had taken important measures to address worsened fiscal and external positions, while the program continued to require a market-determined exchange rate, prudent monetary policy, and structural reforms to improve SOEs and governance.
evidence.title: IMF Executive Board Completes the Combined Seventh, and Eighth Reviews of the Extended Fund Facility for Pakistan
evidence.excerpt: The IMF said Pakistan's authorities had taken important measures to address worsened fiscal and external positions, while the program continued to require a market-determined exchange rate, prudent monetary policy, and structural reforms to improve SOEs and governance.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Primary IMF review with both retrospective and forward-looking policy assessment.
evidence.period_fit: Directly within 2022 and after the first phase of Sharif's economic turnaround effort.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Attributed to the Sharif government and its program implementation, but constrained by Ukraine spillovers, inflation, and prior policy choices.
contrary_evidence: The same IMF review attributed FY22 deficits and reserve erosion to procyclical domestic policies and external shocks.

evidence.claim: Pakistan appointed career central banker Jameel Ahmad as governor of the State Bank of Pakistan for a five-year term, and he was expected to chair a monetary-policy meeting soon after taking office.
evidence.title: Pakistan picks central bank veteran Jameel Ahmad as new governor
evidence.excerpt: Pakistan appointed career central banker Jameel Ahmad as governor of the State Bank of Pakistan for a five-year term, and he was expected to chair a monetary-policy meeting soon after taking office.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Reuters reporting on a specific high-level appointment with institutional facts about the appointee.
evidence.period_fit: Directly within 2022 and relevant to the Sharif government's macro-management decisions.
evidence.ruler_attribution: The governor was appointed by the Sharif government, but the SBP remained an institutionally separate actor.
contrary_evidence: Appointment quality does not by itself prove the quality of later monetary policy.

evidence.claim: Miftah Ismail resigned as finance minister, clearing the way for Ishaq Dar to take over after months of internal pressure about key economic decisions, especially fuel prices.
evidence.title: Miftah resigns as finance minister to pave way for Dar
evidence.excerpt: Miftah Ismail resigned as finance minister, clearing the way for Ishaq Dar to take over after months of internal pressure about key economic decisions, especially fuel prices.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Contemporaneous local reporting on a specific cabinet turnover and the reasons attached to it.
evidence.period_fit: Directly within the target period and after the first half-year of Sharif's tenure.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Attributable to Sharif's coalition and party leadership choices; the precise degree of PM autonomy is partly obscured by party-family dynamics.
contrary_evidence: The resignation also reflects coalition and party politics rather than a clean managerial judgment.

evidence.claim: Ishaq Dar took oath as finance minister while Pakistan was facing a balance-of-payments crisis, foreign reserves near one month of imports, a tumbling rupee, and inflation above 27 percent.
evidence.title: Pakistan swears in Ishaq Dar as finance minister
evidence.excerpt: Ishaq Dar took oath as finance minister while Pakistan was facing a balance-of-payments crisis, foreign reserves near one month of imports, a tumbling rupee, and inflation above 27 percent.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Reuters report with clear contemporaneous macro facts and a high-level appointment event.
evidence.ruler_attribution: The appointment was made under Sharif's government, but the macro conditions were inherited and also shaped by global shocks.
contrary_evidence: The crisis predated Dar's appointment, so the article does not isolate Sharif's own economic competence.

evidence.claim: The IMF program materials said strengthening governance and control of corruption remained key, including an electronic asset-declaration system and a review of anticorruption institutions such as NAB.
evidence.title: Pakistan: 2021 Article IV Consultation, Sixth Review Under the Extended Arrangement Under the Extended Fund Facility, and Requests for Waivers...
evidence.excerpt: The IMF program materials said strengthening governance and control of corruption remained key, including an electronic asset-declaration system and a review of anticorruption institutions such as NAB.
evidence.source_locator: paragraph 27 in the IMF staff report snippet
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Primary IMF program document with concrete governance benchmarks, though the full article page was blocked for direct open in this environment.
evidence.period_fit: The commitment was part of the 2022 IMF program context and remained relevant during Sharif's tenure.
evidence.ruler_attribution: The commitments were made by the Pakistani authorities under the Sharif-led coalition; implementation timing and completeness remained uncertain.
contrary_evidence: This is a program commitment rather than proof that the anti-corruption reforms were fully implemented in 2022.

evidence.claim: Pakistan's annual inflation was still 23.8 percent in November after 26.6 percent in October, showing that price pressures remained severe despite policy tightening.
evidence.title: Pakistan's consumer price inflation slows to 23.8%
evidence.excerpt: Pakistan's annual inflation was still 23.8 percent in November after 26.6 percent in October, showing that price pressures remained severe despite policy tightening.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Reuters reporting on official inflation data and central-bank reaction.
evidence.period_fit: Late 2022 and directly relevant to year-end macro management.
evidence.ruler_attribution: The inflation outcome was partly inherited and partly affected by global shocks and floods, but the government's policy response is still attributable.
contrary_evidence: The month-to-month decline shows some stabilization, so this is mixed rather than pure failure.

unresolved_gaps: No independent 2022 evidence of a Sharif-chaired NCA session or any doctrine, custody, or command-and-control reform.
No direct evidence of Sharif's handling of dual-use, proliferation, cyber, biosecurity, or AI-risk policy in 2022.
The April 2022 Afghanistan strike allegation remains unresolved by an independent finding or clear attribution chain.
No formal ceasefire or settlement output with India or Afghanistan beyond public diplomacy and border-management statements.
Primary court orders or audit findings on the Ramzan Sugar Mills and Ashiana matters are still needed to separate allegations from a durable personal-nexus finding.
The appointment/favoritism question still lacks stronger evidence about whether key personnel choices reflected merit or protection of insiders.
